sections.h2: Who to call in McLean County
sections.html:
A question about what your property is worth belongs with the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA). A question about paying the bill belongs with the Sheriff. Letters to the PVA go to P.O. Box 246, Calhoun, KY 42327, and the phone is (270) 273-3291. The Sheriff's Office is at 135 East 2nd Street in Calhoun, and you can reach online tax records through a link on the Sheriff's page of the county site.

These are separate counters. January 1 values and exemption forms sit with the PVA, which can't accept a payment. The Sheriff takes money until April 15, then hands what is left to the County Clerk. Whether the house is in Calhoun, Livermore, Island, Sacramento or out in the country, these are the same two offices.

KRS 134.015 sets the steps. The cost of an unpaid bill rises like this:

McLean County bill by payment date
Payment windowAmount owed
Through November 12 percent off
Rest of the yearPrinted amount
January5 percent extra
February through April 1510 percent extra

On April 15 the Sheriff's role ends and any open bill moves to the County Clerk. If bills are mailed late, the state revenue department can switch to a slower schedule with one month each at discount, face value and the 5 percent penalty. Either way, unpaid tax is the taxpayer's own debt, backdated to the assessment date.

sections.h2: What an owner can expect to pay
sections.html:
The Census median home value is $148,500, and the state's 2025 rate is 10.6 cents per $100 of assessed value. The fiscal court, schools and other districts each levy their own rate on top, so the real bill is higher. A PVA clerk can total the rates for one address.

This county has been losing residents since 1910, when 13,241 people lived here. The 2020 count was 9,152, and 2025 is estimated at 9,064 people in 3,641 households. That slow decline limits the number of buyers. About 82.8 percent of homes are owner-occupied and median rent is $641. Just two building permits were issued in 2025, which means buyers are nearly always shopping for an existing house.

Every Kentucky county has one. A deduction of $49,100 from assessed value covers 2025 and 2026 for anyone who is 65 or older or has been found totally disabled. About 22.5 percent of McLean residents are 65 or older, so many households qualify.

Take a driver's license, birth certificate or passport to the PVA when you apply. Disability claims need a government or pension finding and renew every year. Owners with a service-connected disability, and people Social Security or the Kentucky Retirement Systems has ruled permanently and totally disabled, skip the renewal. When the house sells, tell the PVA so the deduction comes off the old address.

Your first stop is the PVA. The board of assessment appeals listens only to owners who made that visit. After it, the calendar runs like this:

  • The roll is open for 13 days from the first Monday in May. The county's largest newspaper advertises the dates.
  • At the meeting, the PVA explains your number and a form records the conversation.
  • File the appeal with the County Clerk before closing time on the business day after inspection ends.
  • Bring paper: land and building descriptions, insurance records, construction costs, and listings or sales of similar property. Bare claims are rejected.

The board sits about a month later and owes you written reasons for any change. A paid representative must come from the state's list of professions and show your written authority. If you skip the hearing, the Kentucky Claims Commission is off the table.

A tax lien stays with the parcel no matter who sells it. After April 15 the County Clerk carries open bills as certificates of delinquency, records the lien and starts charging 1 percent a month. Under KRS 134.420 the lien lasts 11 years and binds the next owner too.

Charges pile up in layers. The Clerk adds 10 percent and the county attorney adds 20 percent once notices go out, with postage, advertising and lien fees besides. Ask the Sheriff for a payoff figure until April 15 and the Clerk after that. A certificate can be auctioned 90 to 135 days after the transfer, and the buyer may add charges of their own.

Have the payoff in writing before you accept an offer. The closing agent pays it out of the sale money, so it sets what you net.

sections.h2: Selling a home in McLean County
sections.html:
McLean County was formed on February 6, 1854 from parts of Daviess, Ohio and Muhlenberg counties. It covers 256 square miles of the Western Coal Fields inside the Owensboro metropolitan area, and the Green River crosses it from southeast to northwest. Calhoun is the seat and Livermore is the largest community. The county is dry, so alcohol sales are prohibited. One county-wide school district serves the whole county.

Median household income is $65,596 and the average commute is 31.4 minutes, which suggests many workers drive out of the county, with Owensboro the nearest big job market. Anyone with an inherited house, a rural parcel or tax still owing can sell for cash as-is. Collect the payoff from the Sheriff and the parcel record from the PVA before naming a price.

Three offices each keep a different record on one parcel, so check with all of them before you pick a closing date. The PVA can confirm the acreage, owner name and any homestead claim. The Sheriff or Clerk, depending on the calendar, gives the payoff. The County Clerk records the deed and any lien.

Have a photo ID and your latest bill handy when you call. A property that came from an estate needs the papers showing who may sign. After closing, let the PVA know the new owner's name so the next bill is mailed correctly and the old exemption ends.

If the house is vacant or needs work, a buyer who pays cash as-is can close without repairs, inspections that depend on lender rules, or a long wait. That can matter when a bill is close to turning delinquent and the penalty steps are counting down. Ask each office what it needs in writing, since a verbal quote is hard to rely on at the closing table.

For an inherited house, find out early who holds the deed and whether any bill from earlier years is still open. Old balances can sit on the parcel for years, and they show up at the payoff request. Sorting this out before listing keeps a sale from stalling after you have signed a contract.

faqs.q: Does the McLean County PVA take payments?
faqs.a: No. Call the PVA at (270) 273-3291 about assessments and exemptions, and pay the Sheriff.

faqs.q: When does a McLean County bill turn delinquent?
faqs.a: The 10 percent penalty starts when January ends. After April 15 the County Clerk gets any open bill, adds a lien and begins monthly interest of 1 percent.

faqs.q: What is the McLean County homestead exemption worth?
faqs.a: It cuts $49,100 from assessed value for 2025 and 2026. People 65 or older, or totally disabled, apply with the PVA in Calhoun.

faqs.q: What rate does the state charge?
faqs.a: The state's 2025 rate is 10.6 cents per $100 of assessed value. Local taxing bodies add their own rates.

faqs.q: Who decides a McLean County assessment appeal?
faqs.a: A local board made up of area property owners. It meets about a month after the roll inspection, and you file through the County Clerk once you have seen the PVA.
